answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded stake per identity. Each clone must post its own bond up front, and the slashing sweep strips it once the clone graph is exposed. Even at the nadir of an attack, cost scales with clone count while reward per clone falls as emissions dilute across a widening grove of lookalikes. A bond is cheap to post but costly to lose once accounts link to a wharf of siblings via shared payouts. Identity is priced: fabricating many means paying many times, each payment at risk. The defender pays one audit; the attacker pays a bond per fake agent plus the stake when caught.
